Subject: Follow-up: Logging controls & sensitive data redaction (post-demo)

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our demo and the action items we discussed: 

1) Scope of logs: Redwood keeps request/response logs for the purpose of debugging and performance analysis. By default, these logs include metadata (timestamps, route/model, latency, request id/trace id) but request/response bodies are not persisted unless a customer enables full request logging.

2) Sensitive data redaction: We offer automatic redaction rules for common PII patterns (SSNs, credit card numbers, email addresses) at ingestion and at rest. Customers can also provide custom redaction regexes and configure redaction at the prefix (prompt) or full-response level.

3) Retention & residency: Default retention window for debug logs is 30 days; we can configure retention windows per customer (e.g., 7/30/90/365 days) and support region-restricted storage for US/EU workloads.

4) Headers & trace IDs: Headers containing sensitive values (e.g., Authorization) are dropped from logs by default. Trace IDs and request ids are kept to link traces but can be hashed or tokenized on ingest per customer policy.

Next steps (we agreed):
- I will send a short technical note describing the logging controls, redaction options, and how they map to SOC2/PCI requirements (by EOD PT). (ACTION: Marissa)
- FintechCo to confirm whether you need request/response bodies persisted for any compliance or observability reasons, and your preferred retention window. (ACTION: Samir/Priya)
- Loop in Redwood security for an architecture review if you want to move forward with a Dedicated or Private deployment. (ACTION: Marissa -> will introduce Neha)

Thanks Marissa — great session. A couple quick clarifying questions from our security team so we can move to procurement:

Hi Samir — thanks for the questions. Short answers below and a couple of config examples attached. I'll also loop Neha (Redwood security) for the deeper architecture Qs.

- Redaction timing: We support both — default is pre-persist redaction at ingestion for our managed offering. That means PII patterns are masked before logs are written to disk. For Private deployments we provide the same agents but customers can choose where the redaction runs.

- Trace ID handling: We support hashing/tokenization of trace IDs at ingestion. You can choose to keep the original trace id for a configured nonce window or store only the hashed id; the hashing algorithm and salt are customer-configurable for Dedicated/Private deployments.

- Short-term request/response logging: Yes. You can enable ephemeral request body logging scoped to a workspace and set a TTL (e.g., 24/72 hours). We also support routing those artifacts to a customer-managed S3 bucket (us-west-2) via our secure transfer connector; the transfer happens within a configurable retention window and then the logs are deleted from Redwood storage per your TTL.

Config snippets (attached):
- redaction config: how to add custom regex, scope (prompt/response/headers), and default masking token.
- retention config: sample workspace policy (ttl_days: 30 / ephemeral_ttl: 72)
- s3 connector: manifest for routing ephemeral logs to customer S3 with kms key reference.

We'll also attach an excerpt mapping these controls to SOC2 common criteria. If you'd like a short architecture walk-through, Neha can join a quick call tomorrow.

Best,
Marissa
